name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 application and reusable server implementation for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), built on the Machai AI framework. It bridges MCP-compatible clients with Machai functional tools and prompts, supporting discovery, schema adaptation, request routing, and execution of extension-provided capabilities. It can run locally over STDIO or remotely over HTTP, with stateless HTTP and session-aware streamable HTTP modes. The server does not bundle domain tools; applications add functional-tool and prompt libraries on the runtime classpath and provide any required configuration, credentials, models, or services. It supports tool filtering through enabledTools, configurable server identity, and project-directory context. The project is packaged as a Maven artifact and offers a pack profile for an executable jar with dependencies.

usageContext: STDIO integration with local AI clients
HTTP integration with remote MCP clients

features.name: getEnabledTools
features.description: Reads the optional enabled-tool list from server configuration. Tool names can be separated by spaces, commas, semicolons, or whitespace. Returns null when no restriction is configured, otherwise returns the enabled tool names.

examples.description: A server subclass can expose the protected configuration helper to its integration code and use its resulting tool names to configure tool discovery. In a concrete implementation, provide the configurator loaded by the application.

features.name: setProjectDir
features.description: Sets the project directory used as context by server tools. Pass null when the project directory should be determined for each request.

examples.description: Set a fixed workspace directory before starting a customized server so tools that operate on project files use the intended project context.

features.name: getProjectDir
features.description: Returns the configured project directory, or null when the directory is determined for each request.

examples.description: Read the configured workspace and convert it to a java.nio.file.Path when implementing project-aware tool behavior.

features.name: MCP server launch and transport selection
features.description: Launches the MCP server application. Without --port it uses STDIO; supplying --port enables HTTP. HTTP is stateless by default, and --session selects streamable session-aware transport. Runtime functional-tool and prompt libraries are supplied separately.

examples.description: On Windows, place the executable server distribution and an extension library on the classpath, configure a project workspace and properties file, then run a streamable HTTP MCP endpoint on port 45000. Omit --port for STDIO or --session for stateless HTTP. Set environment variables and credentials required by the extension tools before launching.

customizations.name: AbstractMcpServer extension point
customizations.description: Base abstract implementation for custom MCP server implementations. It provides common server hooks, constants, and project-directory management, allowing specialized servers to build on shared MCP behavior.

examples.description: Extend the abstract base class in a Java application to customize server behavior while reusing project-directory context support. Implement any abstract requirements applicable to the selected library version.

customizations.name: enabledTools configuration property
customizations.description: Optional setting that restricts the tools loaded by the server. Names can be separated with whitespace, commas, or semicolons. When omitted, the server does not request an enabled-tool restriction.

examples.description: Place this property in the server configuration file to limit discovery to the listed tool names; replace these illustrative names with tools published by runtime extension libraries.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer
studs.description: Base class defining shared hooks and project-directory management for custom Model Context Protocol server implementations.

examples.description: Subclass the abstract server base in an extension and set a workspace directory for tools requiring project context.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run a Windows HTTP MCP server
steps: Install a Java 17 or later JDK and download the machai-mcp-server 1.4.3 release jar with dependencies from the project releases, or build it with Maven using the pack profile.
Prepare a separate Machai-compatible functional-tool or prompt extension jar and put both jars on the runtime classpath; the server distribution does not include domain-specific tools.
Create a properties file containing mcp.server.name=my-mcp-server, mcp.server.version=1.0.0, and enabledTools=project_search,code_review, replacing sample names with real extension tool names.

Set credentials and environment configuration required by the selected tools, then invoke org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer with --projectDir, --config, --port 45000, and optionally --session.
Connect an MCP client to http://localhost:45000/mcp and discover and invoke the exposed tools.
examples.description: End-to-end installation and operation for a Windows deployment. Use a classpath containing the server and extension libraries, configure application properties and any provider-specific environment variables, run the HTTP server, and connect an MCP client to its endpoint.

examples.title: Run locally over STDIO
examples.description: Add the server and tool extension jars to the classpath and configure the MCP client to start this command as a child process. STDIO is selected when --port is not supplied. Configure provider credentials in the client process environment as required by the tools.

examples.title: Build the executable distribution
steps: Install Maven and a Java 17 JDK.
Set MACHANISM_PACK_DIR to a writable output directory.
Run mvn -Ppack install from the project root to create the jar-with-dependencies release distribution.
examples.description: The Maven pack profile assembles an executable jar with dependencies under the configured pack directory. Add required tool extension jars and their own configuration when deploying the server.
